subtitle: When BTC dumps, correlations across all alts spike toward 1.0. Independent technical setups stop working. A book of 5 "diversified" longs becomes one trade with five names. Understanding cascade dynamics is the difference between survival and account-wide blowup.

blocks.content: You learned about correlation regimes in lesson 44. This lesson goes deeper into the specific case that hurts retail traders most: the risk-off cascade. It's when a single trigger (BTC dump, macro news, exchange issue) causes correlations to spike across the entire crypto universe — and every long position you hold starts losing simultaneously.

In normal conditions, BTC and alts are moderately correlated (typically 0.5-0.7). Different sector alts (DeFi, gaming, AI, memes) often decorrelate from each other — DeFi can rally while memes dump.

When risk-off hits, correlations spike to 0.85-0.95. Suddenly every coin moves together. The reasons:

  • Margin calls cascade — leveraged longs in any coin start getting liquidated, forcing sell pressure across the board
  • Risk-off algorithms — institutional traders dump everything when BTC breaks key levels
  • Retail panic — "sell everything" psychology overwhelms individual setups
  • Stablecoin flight — money rotates from positions to USDT/USDC, drawing liquidity from all books

In a cascade, your portfolio doesn't lose at the same time — it loses in SEQUENCE. The position with the tightest SL goes first. Then the next one. Then the next. Each one fires roughly 30-90 minutes apart as the wave moves through the book.

Real example from 2026-05-28 overnight:
Four coins stopped within 3 hours. The five longs collectively lost $192. The single short HEDGE gained $6.55 — only +3% of the long losses, but directionally correct.

blocks.title: Diversification is partial protection
blocks.content:
Holding 5 different alts doesn't mean 5 independent risks. In a cascade, they're 1 trade × 5 names. A truly diversified portfolio mixes:

  • Direction — some longs, some shorts (the FIL hedge)
  • Asset class — crypto + some non-crypto if possible
  • Timeframe — some short-term, some long-term

Without direction-diversification, your alt longs are just one big BTC long with extra steps.

A small short position in a high-conviction bearish setup can offset 5-15% of long losses in a cascade. Math:

  • 5 longs total notional $3000, average drops 5% in dump = $150 loss
  • 1 short notional $500, gains 5% from dump = $25 gain
  • Net: $125 loss instead of $150 — 17% mitigation

You can't fully hedge a long book with a single short — that defeats the long thesis. But you can REDUCE the cascade impact with a directionally-correct short on the weakest coin.
What to do BEFORE the cascade

blocks.title: Pre-cascade checklist
blocks.content:
1. SL on every position — no exceptions, no "I'll watch it manually"
  2. Wick-safe SL placement — 0.5-1.0× ATR_4H below the recent 10-bar low (see SL placement lesson)
  3. Sum your worst-case — if every SL fires, what's the dollar loss? Keep it under 5% of equity
  4. Hold a small short hedge in the weakest coin (deep_overbought + gold_sell)
  5. Position size for cascade scenario — not just for the best case
What to do DURING the cascade

The temptation when 3 positions just stopped: "buy the dip" on the 4th. RESIST. The cascade isn't over until correlation normalises. Adding longs into a falling cascade compounds losses.

If you must act, the ONLY two productive actions:

  • Add to the SHORT hedge — the trend is now confirmed
  • Close remaining longs early — accept the loss before SL hits, free capital for after

Stay away from adding longs until the macro filter (MTF EMA) shows a clear regime change.
What to do AFTER the cascade

Once price stabilises and the dump pressure exhausts, the next 6-12 hours often present the BEST counter-trend long opportunities of the cycle:

  • WT2 has reached deep oversold across most coins
  • RSI is in the 25-35 range
  • Forced sellers (margin calls, panic) have cleared
  • The MTF EMA verdict might still say "trend_up_aging" — the macro thesis isn't broken, just retraced

The Yellow X / Gold Buy setups that appear post-cascade are the highest-probability counter-trend longs of the year. Be patient, wait for the cascade to exhaust, then deploy fresh capital into clean setups.

blocks.title: Slippage during cascades is REAL
blocks.content: During a fast dump, your tick-based SL may fill 1-2% below the trigger price due to thin liquidity and slip. Real example: CHZ SL set at $0.0345 → filled at $0.0339 (~$9 extra loss on a $546 notional). Plan for this — your displayed "worst-case loss" should include a 0.5-1% slippage buffer.

blocks.title: Bottom line
blocks.content: In a cascade, correlations spike, your "diversified" alt longs become one trade with five names, and SLs fire in sequence over 2-4 hours. The best protection is direction-diversification (small short hedge), wick-safe SL placement, and discipline NOT to add longs mid-cascade. Post-cascade exhaustion often presents the best counter-trend longs of the year. Wait for the cascade to end before deploying fresh capital.
